headline: South Asia: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week.
- Africa: Ethiopia: Lethal Artillery Strikes On Civilian Neighbourhoods in Tigray's Alamata City Must Be Investigated As War Crimes.
- Asia: Hamas security chief killed in Israeli air strike on Gaza City.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
- Military Times, one day ago: Trump reluctantly orders Army to pause detonation of unstable ammunition.
Trump said he wanted to move forward with the controlled blasts but is putting the decision in the hands of the courts.
- Military Times, one day ago: B-2 bomber wings awarded Presidential Unit Citation for Midnight Hammer.
The award marks the first time a bomber unit has been recognized with a President Unit Citation since the Vietnam War.
- Military Times, one day ago: Under Hegseth, the OSS rides again — kind of.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth resurrected the OSS, created during the Second World War under "Wild Bill" Donovan.
- Military Times, one day ago: VFW seeks veterans’ input on health care experiences in and out of VA.
Through early January, Veterans of Foreign Wars is conducting a survey of veterans on their health care experiences, including medical treatment received at the Department of Veterans Affairs or in private care.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 23 hours ago: ODPEM fiasco could scare off future donors, PNP warns.
Local and international partners could become reluctant to donate to Jamaica in future national emergencies if confidence in the management of humanitarian aid is not urgently restored, Opposition Spokesperson on Local Government Natalie Neita Garvey has warned. This comes amid findings from a report by the auditor general that the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Emergency Management (ODPEM) misused funds donated for a Government-directed roof programme to clear third-party goods.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 23 hours ago: Wright: They behave like hooligans but want to be called honourable.
WESTERN BUREAU: Amid deepening political rifts that have spilled from Gordon House into the courts, outspoken educator Linvern Wright is accusing some parliamentarians of abandoning principles, fairness and national responsibility in favour of partisan warfare.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 10 hours ago: Argentina officially enters a technical recession.
Despite September's month-over-month growth, poor figures for July and August dragged down quarterly performance. Economists are already warning of “stagflation” La entrada Argentina officially enters a technical recession se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian drone strikes civilian car in Sumy: 76-year-old man killed.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russian drone strikes civilian car in Sumy: 76-year-old man killed.
A Russian fibre-optic FPV drone hit a civilian car in Sumy's Kovpakivskyi district, killing a 76-year-old passenger; his son, the driver, is in hospital.
- The Moscow Times, 14 hours ago: Zelensky Confirms Ukraine Was Behind Drone Attack on Russian Cargo Ship in Gulf of Finland.
Volodymyr Zelensky said the cargo ship Sparta II and "every vessel with a Russian flag" are legitimate targets for Ukrainian strikes.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Ukrainian foreign minister advises Putin to stop complaining about strikes on oil refineries and end war instead.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has responded to Russian ruler Vladimir Putin's complaints about Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, advising him to order an end to the war instead.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 11 hours ago: Number of Russian attacks on Naftogaz facilities since start of war exceeds 800.
Naftogaz says its facilities have been struck more than 800 times since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, but its plants continue producing oil and gas.
Southern Europe - bottom line: ‘Everything that concerns Libya concerns Italy’: Why Ukraine’s Med strike is a problem for Meloni.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: ‘Everything that concerns Libya concerns Italy’: Why Ukraine’s Med strike is a problem for Meloni.
The Italian prime minister is a strong backer of Kyiv, but there is worry in Rome that the strikes on Russian ships could destabilize Libya.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: James Cleverly is ready to run for London mayor. Labour is still waiting on Sadiq Khan..
The incumbent London mayor needs to make up his mind or risk giving opponents a head start, Labour MPs are warning.
- Balkan Insight, 12 hours ago: Belgrade Court Convicts Bosnian Serb Woman of Wartime Killings.
The Higher Court in Belgrade found Visnja Acimovic guilty of involvement in the murder of at least 30 Bosniak civilians in June 1992 in the Vlasenica area during the Bosnian war.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Ethiopia: Lethal Artillery Strikes On Civilian Neighbourhoods in Tigray's Alamata City Must Be Investigated As War Crimes.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one day ago: Ethiopia: Lethal Artillery Strikes On Civilian Neighbourhoods in Tigray's Alamata City Must Be Investigated As War Crimes.
[AI London] Artillery attacks by Ethiopia's military and its allied Tigray Peace Forces (TPF) that killed dozens of civilians and injured many more in the city of Alamata in the northern region of Tigray, between 26 and 28 September, must be investigated as possible war crimes, Amnesty International said today.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 22 hours ago: Nigeria: Military Air Strikes Kill 37 Terrorists, Destroy 4 Vehicles in Borno.
[Leadership] The Nigerian military has intensified its aerial offensive against terrorists in Borno State, with air strikes by Operation HADIN KAI killing 37 terrorists and destroying four vehicles in one week.
- Africanews, 13 hours ago: Colombia: At least 25 injured in bombing as armed violence resurges.
At least 25 people were injured in a bombing in Villavicencio, damaging government buildings, businesses and vehicles. Meanwhile, hundreds of residents marched with candles in Cúcuta following a separate attack, amid a resurgence of armed violence in Colombia.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: Nigeria: Military Air Interdictions Eliminate 37 Terrorists, Destroy Logistics Assets in North-East.
[This Day] Abuja -- The sustained operational pressure exerted by air assets of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), on terrorist elements through a series of intelligence-led precision air strikes across the theatre has resulted in the killing of 37 terrorists and the destruction of their logistics assets, the Nigerian military has said.

The Saudi coalition says its forces targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port and hit sites in northern Yemen.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Rebel group retreats in DR Congo after heavy clashes with government forces.
CRP halts advance towards Bunia, citing commitments made during Ugandan-mediated talks with government.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 7 hours ago: Colombian president blames ex-FARC rebels for car bomb blast.
Colombian President De la Espriella blames the FARC for plotting a bombing that injured tens and pledges to retaliate.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 19 hours ago: Namibia: Life Sentence for 'Gay Ghost' Murder Accused.
[New Era] A Keetmanshop resident who claimed that a gay ghost made sexual advances towards him in his dreams shortly before stabbing his domestic partner to death, has been sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 19 hours ago: Namibia: Jealousy Drove Killer to Stab Ex-Girlfriend 13 Times ... Judge Sentences Offender to 32 Years Imprisonment.
[New Era] Windhoek High Court Acting Judge Marilize du Plessis has described the murder of Auguste Ndemupandula Jonas in 2023 in Otjiwarongo by her alleged former partner as an act of attrition, motivated by pure jealousy after the accused found her with another man.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 19 hours ago: Namibia: Namibia Urges Stronger Enforcement of Child Marriage Laws.
[New Era] Namibian parliamentarian Nelson Kalangula has called for stronger implementation and greater public awareness of laws aimed at eradicating child marriage, saying legislation alone is insufficient without the understanding and support of political, traditional and community leaders.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 19 hours ago: Namibia: Namibia Eyes Bigger Share of Its Uranium Wealth.
[New Era] Namibia is seeking to move beyond exporting uranium and start adding more value to the mineral locally as the government looks to expand the nuclear industry's contribution to the economy.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: 11 injured as Riyadh skyscraper hit second time in less than a week.
Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”. The building, which was also attacked last Thursday, is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Houthis restarted in July. Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence reported Tuesday’s injuries and posted a picture of the landmark tower housing the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF).
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 12 hours ago: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 7, including senior security official.
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials in the territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire in place since last year. Israel’s military said it had struck a senior Hamas official. Gaza’s interior ministry said an airstrike in Gaza City killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahal, director-general of the Internal Security Service. Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, told AFP that several other people were in critical condition following the same strike in Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Balochistan govt announces rewards of up to Rs250m for information on wanted terrorists.
QUETTA: The Balochistan government has announced rewards ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs250 million for providing authentic information about most-wanted terrorists in the province. According to an official advertisement issued by the provincial government, a reward of Rs250m has been fixed for information about Bashir Zeb of the banned Balochistan Liberation Army and Abdul Rehman alias Rehman Gul. Similar rewards have been fixed for other wanted persons depending on their status.
- The Hindu - International, 12 hours ago: A Russian strike on Ukraine kills two, wounds 48 as Kyiv explains its attack in Libya.
A Russian nighttime attack on Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine has killed two civilians and wounded 48 others including four children

Casualties from landmines or unexploded ordnance reached a five-year high in 2025, with Southeast Asia making up a disproportionate number of those killed or wounded, largely due to Myanmar’s civil war, a report released on Tuesday showed. The annual global report by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines found civilians were the most affected, making up some 84 per cent of the 6,929 casualties recorded in 2025, and half of them were children. The Saudi capital’s tallest skyscraper was struck for a second time in days on Tuesday injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis denounced a “terrorist attack”. Three separate witnesses said the strike targeted the 80-storey Public Investment Fund Tower, which houses the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund and dominates Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD). The Chinese military’s PLA Daily reported on Monday that authorities in Guiyang, southwestern China’s Guizhou province, had formed a specialist militia company comprising road and bridge workers from an unnamed major firm involved in building the Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge. India - bottom line: JeM commander acknowledges terror network in Rawalakot.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: JeM commander acknowledges terror network in Rawalakot.
Masood Ilyas Kashmiri has acknowledged the armed presence of Jaish-e-Mohammed in Rawalakot, POK. He criticized the Pakistani authorities for failing to address anti-state activities and violence against paramilitary personnel. Additionally, Ilyas claimed that some JeM members are from the same communities protesting against the government. The Joint Awami Action Committee has urged military operations to cease and warned of a potential uprising.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 11 hours ago: Bezos’ ex-wife gave $62M landmark gift to meet 2030 goals of coastal communities.
MacKenzie Scott has donated $62 million to the marine conservation organization Blue Ventures for their 2030 goals. This donation will support small-scale fishing communities and their efforts in marine ecosystem conservation. The funding aims to enhance local stewardship of carbon-rich seas and improve food security in coastal areas. Blue Ventures will allocate funds through the Frontline Community Fund to empower local partners effectively.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Royal Enfield owner gets Rs 1 lakh copensation as bike's ECU issue disrupts Leh trip.
In a recent ruling, a Delhi consumer commission mandated Eicher Motors to compensate a Noida resident whose Interceptor 650 suffered severe power loss at higher altitudes. Despite the complainant's prior request for an ECU update before his journey, the authorized dealer neglected to take action, leaving the commission with no choice but to side with the complainant, awarding him Rs 1 lakh in compensation for the unaddressed claims.
